newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - May 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - May 28.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In a move which follows intense pressure from the Federal Government and an inquiry into possible collusion by the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission, the ANZ Banking Group yesterday announced its second mortgage rate cut in four days, cutting its variable mortgage rate to 6.99 per cent. Page 1.

Speaking after a Securities Institute of Australia lunch yesterday, Optus Communications chief executive Ziggy Switkowski admitted he was unhappy with aspects of his loss-making pay-TV division Optus Vision, and revealed he had slashed Vision's workforce by 12 per cent since the merger of the companies. Page 25.

In news which follows Rupert Murdoch's News Corp's aborted efforts to acquire EchoStar Communications Corp, News appears to have salvaged its United States satellite television plans, winning a tentative accord to join satellite television group PrimeStar Partners. Page 25.

The long-awaited sale of Sam Linz's 28 per cent interest in Rebel Sport Ltd will be announced today, with about 19 per cent of the stake held by Linz and fellow founding director Robert Gavshon expected to be bought up by one of the four interested partie which have been negotiating for the stake for the last six months. Page 25.

In a result slightly ahead of market expectations, insurance and funds management group National Mutual Holdings has boosted its interim profit by 18.5 per cent to A$176 million on the back of strong equity markets, the continuing turnaround of National Mtual Life and expanded operations in Asia. Page 28.

FAI Insurances Ltd chief executive Rodney Adler said yesterday it is still unaware of the identity of the buyer and seller of large lines of the listed general insurer's shares over the past two days. About 20 million shares were traded on Monday, with 238 million more changing hands yesterday. Page 28.
THE AUSTRALIAN

As part of a huge cost-cutting push designed to integrate Optus Communications and Optus Vision ahead of a share market float, Optus Communications has reduced staff numbers at Vision by 12 per cent, with the decision to take control of Optus Vision resulting in up to 350 jobs being lost within the embattled pay-TV and cable unit. Page 21.

As the market absorbed the full impact of BHP chief executive John Prescott's warning on Monday that the company may suffer a deterioration in final quarter profit, BHP shares slumped 53 cents yesterday to close at A$18.39 - its biggest one-day fall this year - with the company losing a further A$1 billion off its market value. Page 21.

In a positive result for National Mutual Holdings, managing director Tony Killen said it is satisfying for its 5,000-plus shareholders in the group's first half as a listed entity, after the company overcame slow conditions in its life insurance operations to post a net profit of A$176 million for the half-year to March 31. Page 21.

In comments which have been supported by Aussie Home Loans managing director John Symond, Moody's Investors Service's New York-based vice-president Sean Jones said yesterday more bank mergers are inevitable in Australia because of the pressure on interest margins resulting from loan securitisation. Page 23.

Speaking at the annual Foodweek convention in Sydney yesterday, Paul Bourke, the executive director of Prime Minister John Howard's Supermarket to Asia Council, said a large industrial dispute on the waterfront would set back Australia's food export programme to Asia by 20 years. Page 23.

Ford president David Morgan yesterday supported a plan from the head of the Department of Prime Minister and Cabinet Max Moore-Wilton, who is believed to have proposed holding tariffs at 15 per cent from 2000 until 2005 and cutting wholesale sales tax on cars from 22 per cent. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Thanks largely to booming investment markets and a strong performance from its listed Asian subsidiary, National Mutual Holdings, which listed on the Australian Stock Exchange in October, has made a strong debut as a listed company, with interim net profit surging 33.5 per cent to A$175.5 million. Page 29.

As shareholders expressed their disappointment that the benefits expected from BHP's restructuring of its operations would not be realised until 1998, the Big Australian saw its market value stripped by A$1 billion yesterday, with its share price falling 53 cents to A$18.39. Page 29.

Prime Minister John Howard told his Party room yesterday that a decision on car tariffs would be made that was acceptable to both sides of the negotiations, and with Howard departing next month for a two-week overseas trip, a Cabinet decision on a future car industry tariff programme could come as early as next week. Page 29.

The Canadian Government has warned the Australian Government that Federal Treasurer Peter Costello's decision last month to use the Foreign Takeovers Act to order Izzy Asper's CanWest Global Communications to sell down its holding in Network Ten to 57 percent may breach international treaty obligations. Page 29.

In a decision which comes amid the move within the superannuation industry for greater fund choice for members, the Superannuation Trust of Australia yesterday opened its A$1.3 billion low-cost fund open to public subscription, signalling the beginning ofa new era of intense competition between funds for outside members. Page 31.

In a concern that has hatched following intensive discussions between Rupert Murdoch's News Corp and Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting, Optus Communications chief executive Ziggy Switkowski said yesterday the company is concerned PBL and News are planning to shake-up pay-TV without involving all the players. Page 31.
THE AGE

Surging investment markets and a good performance by National Mutual Holding's Asian subsidiary has seen the company debut as a publicly listed company with a profit rise of 33.5 per cent. Despite the result, the market was unmoved with the price of NM shares closing unchanged at $1.95. Page B1.

The Bureau of Statistics reported business investment rose by 6.5 per cent in the seasonally adjusted March quarter, suggesting that economic growth is increasing. However, businesses are still cautious about their investment plans for 1997-98. Page B1.

The Yellow Pages Small Business Index released yesterday found small businesses view big business as an increasing threat. According to the survey, 10 per cent of the 1,200 small businesses questioned identified competition and big business as a major concern, an increase by five per cent from the last survey, two years ago. Page B3.

The Federal Government has the chance to secure its small business support base if it acts quickly on the recommendations outlined in Monday's Reid fair-trading report. The report recommended radical changes to the Trade Practices Act and a uniform Retail tenancy Code to protect against unfair conduct by big business. Page B3.

Japan's Agricultural Ministry has put an immediate ban on Fuji apples from Tasmania because of the outbreak of fire-blight in Victoria. It is predicted the move will spell the end of Tasmania's hopes of opening up an export market to Japan. Page B3.

Ford Australia president David Morgan criticised the Productivity Commission's report into future of Australia's motor industry yesterday, calling it a waste of time and money. Morgan believes the report was predictable, with the Commission becoming close-minded to other points of view. Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
